headline: Gears transform motion—trading speed for force or vice versa
universal_truth: Every system has trade-offs; you can change the form of what you have, not get something for nothing
fun_facts: The Antikythera mechanism, an ancient Greek device from 100 BCE, used intricate gear systems to predict astronomical events
A bicycle's gears let you trade pedaling speed for climbing power—or vice versa
Clock gears slow motion dramatically—the second hand moves thousands of times faster than the hour hand
discussion_questions: How do gears appear in devices you use?
What's being traded when you shift gears on a bike?
Where else in life do you 'shift gears'?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A small gear turns fast. It meshes with a large gear that turns slow—but with more force. Gears are transformers of motion, converting what you have into what you need. Speed becomes force. Force becomes speed.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Gears can increase force or increase speed. But can they do both at once? What law governs what gears can and cannot do?
cliff.prompt: Can gears increase both speed and force?

options.text: No—gears trade one for the other. More force means less speed; more speed means less force
options.response: Yes. Energy is conserved. Gears are transformers, not multipliers. They change the form of motion, not the total amount.

options.text: Yes—that's why gears are so useful in machines
options.response: Gears are useful, but they can't violate physics. They trade speed for force...

q1.title: Ratio Magic
q1.script: Gear ratio determines the trade-off. A small gear driving a large gear increases force but reduces speed. A large gear driving a small one increases speed but reduces force. The ratio tells you exactly how much.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Ratio Magic"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Ancient Precision
q2.script: The Antikythera mechanism, built around 100 BCE, used over 30 intricate bronze gears to model celestial motions. Ancient Greeks understood gear ratios well enough to predict eclipses. Gears enabled the first computers—mechanical ones.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Bicycle Wisdom
q3.script: Your bicycle's gears are a perfect classroom. Low gear: easy pedaling, slow movement, good for hills. High gear: hard pedaling, fast movement, good for flats. You're constantly trading force for speed based on conditions.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Every system has trade-offs. Gears teach that you can transform what you have but not get something for nothing. Understanding trade-offs helps you choose wisely in machines—and in life.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 115. Tomorrow, we'll discover what engines actually do. Until then, notice gears—in bikes, clocks, cars, and countless other machines.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Gear Thinking - Understand Trade-offs
growTrack.activity: Think about a decision you're facing. What's the 'gear ratio'? What are you trading for what? Most choices involve trade-offs like gears—you can shift the balance but can't get everything. What balance works best for you?
